problem: Offline RL needs action labels, but many data sources (videos, other embodiments) only provide state transitions (s,s',r). Naive fixes such as a single imputed action reduce Q-learning to TD(0) policy evaluation, which recovers the behavior policy's value rather than the optimal one. Reconstruction-based prior methods (D3G) do not scale to images.
motivation: Observation-only experience is abundant, and even without knowing actions it says which states are closer to the goal, i.e. the value function V(s). A good value function can densify rewards, guide existing low-level controllers, and transfer across embodiments, so learning it from undirected state-only data is valuable.
key_idea: Mine discrete latent actions with a latent-variable future prediction model (EM-style min over latent actions), then run standard offline Q-learning on the relabeled (s, a_hat, s', r) data to get value functions. Theory says a state-conditioned refinement of the action space preserves the optimal value.
insight: Theorem: Q-learning under any state-conditioned refinement of the action space learns the same optimal value function. The gridworld case study shows that a single action (TD(0)) and noisy, impure actions fail, while a 4x refinement recovers the optimal value. Latent actions from future prediction give higher state-conditioned purity than clustering on images (e.g. Freeway 0.907 vs 0.778/0.773; 3D nav 0.928 vs 0.839/0.859). That translates into higher Spearman correlation with ground-truth-action value functions (3D nav 0.927 vs 0.827 for the best clustering).
method: Latent action mining: a forward model f_theta(o_t, a_hat) with a discrete latent a_hat in a set of 8 (64 for Kitchen) is trained with loss min over a_hat of the L2 error to o_{t+1}, using hard-EM; each transition is then labeled with its argmin a_hat.
Q-learning with latent actions: DQN-style offline Q-learning (or discrete BCQ) on the (o, a_hat, o', r) quadruples; V(s)=max_a Q(s,a). Only the top 3 to 8 dominant latent actions are used.
Densified RL: the learned V is used as a potential-based shaping term F=V(s')-V(s) added to a sparse reward (task reward scaled 5x).
Guiding low-level controllers: at each step pick the hand-designed controller whose predicted next state has the highest V (following Chang et al. 2020).

Cross-embodiment transfer: value functions learned from point-mass or Franka data are queried for an ant or a hook by mapping the state (ant position with zero velocity; end-effector position and environment state).
Extrapolation control: a GMM density model that zeroes V outside the data distribution, or a value re-parameterization 1-||phi(s)||_2, to avoid spuriously high out-of-distribution values.

setting.backbone: MLP / convolutional encoder-decoder forward model + DQN/BCQ Q-networks (trained from scratch, ACME codebase)
setting.training_data: Per-environment state-only offline datasets with action labels discarded: gridworld (20K episodes), Freeway (Agarwal et al. DQN replay protocol, regenerated), Habitat branching-environment trajectories, D4RL Maze2D and FrankaKitchen partial.
setting.observation: Low-dimensional states (xy, xy+velocity, 24-d kitchen state) or RGB images (Freeway 210x160, 224x224 first-person in Habitat)
setting.action_space: Discrete latent actions for Q-learning; the underlying environments use discrete actions (grid, Freeway, nav low-level controllers) or continuous control (Maze2D, Kitchen)
setting.simulator: Habitat (3D nav), D4RL MuJoCo (Maze2D, FrankaKitchen), Atari ALE (Freeway), custom gridworld
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth actions are only used for evaluation reference and BC baselines); rewards are assumed observed

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmark paper. The only navigation-metric result is the SPL in the custom Habitat branching environment. The Spearman correlations (e.g. 3D nav 0.927; Freeway 0.961; Maze2D 0.844; Kitchen 0.905) are in Table 1, and the RL learning curves are figures only, so they are not listed as numbers.
results: LAQ value functions correlate with ground-truth-action value functions (Spearman 0.927 in 3D nav, 0.961 in Freeway), beating clustering alternatives and D3G, and matching or beating them on state-based tasks. As dense rewards they speed up RL over sparse rewards and beat BC with ground-truth actions on undirected data (gridworld, Maze2D), and they transfer to the ant and hook. In the Habitat branching environment, zero-shot control reaches SPL 0.82 vs 0.53 for TD(0) policy evaluation, approaching the inverse-model method (0.95), which needs 40K interaction samples.
limitations: Deterministic latent actions cannot form a strict refinement in stochastic MDPs; the paper proves no algorithm can recover the optimal value from state-only data in general.
Value estimates are only reliable within the data distribution, so out-of-distribution states need density-model or re-parameterization fixes; offline validation (when to stop) remains an issue.
Evaluated on small or synthetic settings; the navigation test is a single custom branching environment with hand-designed low-level controllers.
builds_on: Chang et al. 2020 (Semantic Visual Navigation by Watching YouTube Videos)
compares_to: BC with ground-truth actions (upper bound for BCO/ILPO)
